reasons: No test is visible in the packet.
Errors are shown as text rather than hidden, and missing data shows explicit placeholders.

terms.meaning: A panel that slides in from the edge of the screen.
A record of where a quote came from and how it was checked.
A saved picture of a web page, taken at a point in time.
The computer's copy and paste memory.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the citation panel
sections.what: Brings in the panel frame, external link, data label, snapshot view, icons and link builder.
sections.why: The panel is assembled from these shared parts.

sections.name: CitationLocator
sections.title: Where a quote sits in a source
sections.what: Describes a locator: a type plus an optional value that points to a spot in a source.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets a quote link to its exact place.
sections.watch_out: The type is free text, so unexpected types are not rejected.

sections.name: Citation
sections.title: Shape of one citation
sections.what: Lists the details a citation can carry, such as title, address, publisher, dates, excerpt and locator. Only the id, title and address are required.
sections.why: Defines the data the panel expects.
sections.watch_out: Most fields are optional, so the panel shows placeholders when they are empty.

sections.name: CitationQuote
sections.title: Shape of one full quote
sections.what: Describes one full quote from the evidence list, with its text, address, publisher, date, locator and provenance.
sections.why: The code comment says this matches what the evidence endpoint returns.
sections.watch_out: Text fields can be null, and the panel has to handle that.

sections.name: CitationDrawerProps, TabKey
sections.title: Options the panel accepts
sections.what: Lists what callers can pass in: open state, close handler, the citation, optional full quotes, loading and error states, and the tab to open first.
sections.why: Lets other screens control the panel.
sections.watch_out: Loading takes priority over error, so an error is hidden while loading.

sections.name: CopyButton
sections.title: Copy button with confirmation
sections.what: A button that copies text and changes its label to a confirmation for two seconds.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives the user feedback that copying worked.
sections.watch_out: If both copy methods fail silently, the button still says Copied.

sections.name: VerbatimQuoteBlock (part 1)
sections.title: Quote header and provenance
sections.what: Builds the top of one quote: publisher, date, a provenance note with verification, reading basis and document references, and the quote in a scrolling box. Shows a placeholder when there is no quote.
sections.why: Likely reason: shows where a quote came from and marks report quotes as not publisher wording.
sections.watch_out: Old records may lack document data; bad document data is ignored rather than causing a failure.

sections.name: VerbatimQuoteBlock (part 2)
sections.title: Locator and quote buttons
sections.what: Shows the locator, a copy button for the quote, and a jump link. Says none recorded when there is no locator.
sections.why: Lets the reader find the exact spot in the source.
sections.watch_out: The jump link only appears when the quote has a web address.

sections.name: CitationDrawer (part 1)
sections.title: Drawer state and quote list
sections.what: Keeps the tab, snapshot and copied states. Resets to the first tab on each fresh open. Works out the jump link, and uses the single citation when no full quotes are passed.
sections.why: Likely reason: existing screens get the new tab without changes.
sections.watch_out: The tab and snapshot choice reset whenever the open state or citation id changes, so a user's choice can be lost.

sections.name: CitationDrawer (part 2)
sections.title: Tabs, loading and error views
sections.what: Defines the two tab buttons, then shows loading, an error message, or the citation title and source name.
sections.why: Shows an honest message instead of a made-up citation.
sections.watch_out: The source name is hidden when it matches the title, to avoid repetition.

sections.name: CitationDrawer (part 3)
sections.title: Citation details tab
sections.what: Shows publisher, accessed date, publication date, provenance note, excerpt and an open-source link. Missing values show as not available.
sections.why: Gives the core facts a reader needs to check the source.
sections.watch_out: Not available entries are placeholders, not facts.

sections.name: CitationDrawer (part 4)
sections.title: Copy and jump buttons, snapshot area
sections.what: Shows the copy excerpt button, the jump link, and on the second tab the snapshot area. A real capture appears when a source address exists; otherwise a note says nothing can be captured.
sections.why: Likely reason: no fake image is shown when there is no source.
sections.watch_out: The snapshot comes from the selected quote, or the first quote that has an address.

sections.name: CitationDrawer (part 5)
sections.title: Quote list and snapshot switch
sections.what: Lists each full quote with a divider, and a button to show that quote's snapshot. Shows a no citation selected message when nothing is chosen.
sections.why: Lets a reader switch between several sources for one field.
sections.watch_out: The snapshot is matched by id, so duplicate ids could show the wrong snapshot.

summary: A side panel that shows full details of one citation: title, publisher, dates, excerpt, a link to the source, and a second tab with full quotes, provenance and a page snapshot.
purpose: Lets a reader check a claim against its source without leaving the current page.
why: Likely reason: one shared panel keeps citations looking the same across the app.
how: Shows a loading message, then an error message, or the citation. Two tabs follow: Citation for the details, and Read and Validate for full quotes. Each quote shows provenance, copy and jump buttons, and a snapshot. Copy falls back to an older browser method if the modern one fails.
inputs: Whether the panel is open, a close handler, one citation or nothing, optional full quotes, a loading flag, an error message, and which tab opens first.
outputs: A slide-in panel with tabs, copy buttons and links. It does not save anything.
risks: The fallback copy method is deprecated and may stop working in future browsers. Some quotes are report quotations rather than publisher wording; the panel labels this, but a reader could still overlook it.
debug: If the panel is blank, check the loading and error flags first. If a snapshot slot is empty, check whether the quote has a web address. If a jump link is missing, check the locator and the excerpt.
